domain_symbols.materials_science: solid-state, mechanical, and condensed matter formulas
domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: Hooke's law (isotropic)
rules.input_form: stress sigma, strain epsilon, Young's modulus E
rules.operation: Relate uniaxial stress and strain in the elastic regime.
common_errors: Confusing engineering and true stress at large strains

rules.name: Generalized Hooke's law (anisotropic)
rules.input_form: stress sigma_ij, strain epsilon_kl, stiffness C_ijkl
preconditions: Linear elasticity, C symmetric under (ij<->kl) and minor symmetries
rules.operation: Use the fourth-rank stiffness tensor for anisotropic linear elasticity.
examples: Cubic crystals have 3 independent constants C11, C12, C44
counterexamples: Materials beyond elastic limit need plasticity models
common_errors: Ignoring symmetry-induced zeros in C reduces to fewer constants

rules.name: Von Mises yield criterion
rules.input_form: deviatoric stress s_ij, yield strength sigma_y
rules.output_form: yields when sqrt(3/2 s_ij s_ij) >= sigma_y
rules.operation: Predict yielding under multiaxial stress states for ductile metals.
common_errors: Applying von Mises to brittle materials

rules.name: Griffith fracture criterion
rules.input_form: crack length a, surface energy gamma, modulus E
rules.operation: Predict critical fracture stress for a crack of given length.
common_errors: Ignoring plastic zone size relative to crack length

rules.name: Bragg's law
rules.input_form: spacing d, wavelength lambda, angle theta
rules.operation: Predict X-ray diffraction angles from crystal lattice spacing.
examples: XRD identification of phases in alloys
counterexamples: Amorphous materials show broad halos, not peaks
common_errors: Forgetting that only allowed (hkl) by structure factor give peaks

rules.name: Hall-Petch grain strengthening
rules.input_form: grain size d, constants sigma_0, k
rules.operation: Predict yield strength increase as grain size decreases.
examples: Cold-worked steels show classic Hall-Petch behavior
counterexamples: Inverse Hall-Petch below ~10 nm due to grain-boundary sliding
common_errors: Extrapolating to nanocrystalline regime without correction

rules.name: Arrhenius diffusion
rules.operation: Predict temperature dependence of diffusion or reaction rates.
examples: Carbon diffusion in austenite during carburizing
counterexamples: Quantum tunneling at low T departs from Arrhenius
common_errors: Using inconsistent units of R (J/mol K vs eV/K)

rules.name: Gibbs phase rule
rules.output_form: F = C - P + 2 (intensive degrees of freedom)
preconditions: Equilibrium, no chemical reactions beyond components
rules.operation: Count degrees of freedom in multi-phase equilibria.
examples: Triple point of water: C=1, P=3 -> F=0
counterexamples: Constrained variables (e.g., fixed pressure) reduce F by 1
common_errors: Forgetting to subtract one when pressure is fixed

rules.name: Free electron Fermi energy
rules.operation: Estimate Fermi energy of a metal from electron density.
common_errors: Ignoring effective mass in real solids

rules.name: Semiconductor intrinsic carrier density
rules.input_form: band gap E_g, temperature T, effective DOS N_c, N_v
rules.output_form: n_i = sqrt(N_c N_v) exp(-E_g / (2 k_B T))
rules.operation: Compute intrinsic carrier concentration as a function of temperature.
counterexamples: Heavily doped semiconductors are degenerate (use Fermi integrals)
common_errors: Using room-temperature N_c, N_v at high T without scaling

rules.name: Lindemann melting criterion
rules.operation: Estimate the melting temperature from atomic vibration amplitude.
counterexamples: Glasses do not have a sharp melting transition
common_errors: Assuming delta_L is exactly universal across all crystal classes

rules.name: Curie-Weiss susceptibility
rules.input_form: temperature T, Curie temperature T_C, constant C
rules.output_form: chi = C / (T - T_C) for T > T_C
rules.operation: Describe paramagnetic susceptibility diverging at the Curie point.
counterexamples: Critical region near T_C shows non-mean-field exponents
